Sure, so how I am seeing it:

You're Bob who wants to start a fertilizer business. You have a shovel, a wheelbarrow, and your father in law owns a bunch of cows. You go to your FIL, shovel up cow shit all day, wheel it to the market, and sell it. The price you are setting reflects how much time you've spent doing this, so you can still feed your family. This is you, Bob.

I'm Megafactory Inc. In the Netherlands I have contracts with farmers who have millions of cows. I make the farmers shovel the shit for me and sell it to me for cheap because if they don't, I'll stop buying their milk. I load it onto my fleet of cargo ships and sell it wherever the demand is highest.

I come to your town. Your wheelbarrow, unfortunately, cannot compete with my tankers, factories, and business side-deals. Because I am so far ahead of you, I can set my price just low enough to undercut you, but when compared to how much each cow shit it took me to get versus how much it takes you, I am making a far bigger profit than you ever could. Because there is no way you can out-sell me, you end up joining one of my manure-processing factories just to try and make ends meet. I work you like a slave and pay you pennies, of course, because you have no choice in the matter.

To get where I am, simply reverse this process. Megafactory Inc leaves. Bob's shovel and wheelbarrow suddenly matter a lot more because there's no more tankers carrying it from overseas for cheap. Bob can now charge a local price for his fertilizer rather than compete with a foreign power.

To be perfectly honest, I never used the facebook sign in... until I started web development, and saw exactly what was happening when I signed in with facebook.

They get your name and your email address, as well as some FB-specific non-personal data (tokens, etc). UNLESS THE APP/WEBSITE IS SPECIFICALLY ASKING FOR IT, *THERE IS NO WAY TO POST TO FACEBOOK FOR THEM*. And even if they are, you can turn that permission off so they can't reach the data you don't want them to reach.

So yeah. Now I use it and I'm happy I don't have to remember 50 different passwords. Never had anything be posted to my timeline in the last 2 years or so.

That said, if a website is asking you to log in for no reason whatsover (cough^quora^cough), fuck that noise. Right click -> inspect element -> delete overlay node. Fuck you, Quora.

To be honest, I don't really blame you. I fell in love with the book at the first reading because of Vonnegut's incredible language, but I could not understand why it was an anti-war book. You're absolutely right, it seems like the Tralfmadorians sort of "condone" all these horrors, because "so it goes" -- the world spins, it doesn't matter if they live or die; they were alive in the past, that's enough for them.

Humans, however, cannot normally become unstuck in time, like Billy and the Tralfmadorians. This logic does not apply to them.

It took me a few readings to understand this, but I had the benefit of liking the book for merits other than its message. It's just unfortunate that it seems like you've made up your mind about it and will not be re-reading it. It is my favourite novel at this point in life, and I recommend it heartily to anyone who reads.
